features.title: Core capabilities
features.desc: Built for the way media teams actually work, feature by feature

transcribe.title: AI transcription
transcribe.desc: Whisper runs on your own machine: the text appears line by line, with no upload and no waiting. 12 languages, and the fast/precise tier is your call.

playback.title: Line-by-line playback
playback.desc: Click a subtitle and playback starts at that line; the line being spoken highlights itself. Drag the seek bar, edit the wording and each line's start and end times right in the row.

progress.title: Progress and cancel
progress.desc: Transcription reports a real percentage, voice-over counts segments ("X of N synthesized"), and both can be stopped halfway. A call already sent cannot be recalled.

reference.title: Reference script diff
reference.desc: Upload the broadcast or reference script and it is diffed word by word against the transcript, so every difference stands out.

correction.title: Two ways to proofread
correction.desc: Local proofreading runs on the built-in misheard-word list and Chinese dictionary: no setup, no network. AI proofreading explains each difference in context. Both only propose fixes - you accept them one by one.

voice.title: Subtitle voice-over
voice.desc: Turn finished subtitles into a voice track you can actually use: synthesized segment by segment, laid onto the subtitle timeline as a single MP3. The voice-over step itself leaves your subtitles and their timing untouched.

privacy.title: Local by default
privacy.desc: In local mode transcription and comparison stay on your machine. Files never go to the cloud, so your material stays confidential.

download.title: Video download
download.desc: Paste a public video link: once the app resolves the duration and the available qualities, choose between transcribing the audio and downloading the video. Some sites block hotlinking.

export.title: Multi-format export
export.desc: Export to SRT, VTT, TSV, TXT, JSON or Markdown - six formats that drop straight into your post-production pipeline.

flow.title: Three steps, that is all
flow.desc: From raw audio-video to clean subtitles in minutes

import.title: Import media
import.desc: Drag in a local audio or video file, pick one from disk, or paste a URL to download it first. Mainstream formats such as mp4, mp3 and wav are supported.

run.title: Let AI transcribe
run.desc: The local Whisper engine transcribes at full speed with live progress. When it finishes you can upload a reference script to compare against.

review.title: Compare and proofread
review.desc: Subtitles are diffed against the reference automatically. Click Proofread, pick local or AI, review each suggestion, then export.

overview.intro: Vv Transcribe is an AI subtitle transcription and proofreading tool for media professionals. It runs the local Whisper speech recognition engine to transcribe audio and video quickly, then adds reference script comparison plus both local and AI proofreading, so broadcast teams can proofread captions precisely and keep mistakes off air.
overview.card1Desc: Files never go to the cloud
overview.card2Desc: Open-source engine, no paid API needed
overview.card3Desc: Export SRT / VTT / TSV / TXT / JSON / Markdown

install.winText: Windows 10 or 11, 64-bit. 8GB of RAM or more is recommended.
install.macText: macOS 12 or later, on both Intel and Apple Silicon (any M-series chip).
install.diskText: The installer is about 311MB (Apple silicon) / 352MB (Intel Mac) / 416MB (Windows) and already includes the link transcription component. The first transcription then downloads the model weights for the tier you picked - about 138MB for the default Fast tier, about 461MB for Precise.
install.step1: Download the installer for your system from this site (Windows .exe / macOS .dmg).
install.step2: Run the installer and follow the prompts.
install.step3: On the first transcription the app downloads the Whisper model (by default the Fast tier, base, about 138MB; if you switch to the Precise tier small under Settings → Transcription it is about 461MB) - please wait for it.
install.step4: Once the model is cached you are ready to work.
install.brewLead: On macOS you can also install it with Homebrew:
install.brewNoteLead: Since Homebrew 7 you must trust a tap before third-party formula files can be loaded; to pick up a later version use
install.brewNoteTail: - the cask tracks latest, so brew upgrade will not offer it.
install.warnTitle: First launch says the developer cannot be verified, the app is damaged, or Windows protected your PC?
install.warnIntro: This is expected. Vv Transcribe is a personal open-source project and does not yet have a paid code-signing certificate, so the system blocks the first launch. The app itself is safe and complete, and in local mode transcription and comparison never leave this computer. Work through the steps below in order - each is a one-time action:
install.warn1Text: Dismiss the cannot-open dialog, then open **System Settings → Privacy & Security**. Scroll to the very bottom, find the line saying Vv Transcribe was blocked, and click **"Open Anyway"** next to it. You may need your login password.
install.warn2Text: Open the Applications folder, **right-click** Vv Transcribe, choose Open, then click Open in the dialog.
install.warn3Label: If it says the app is damaged and cannot be opened:
install.warn3Text: That comes from the quarantine attribute the download added. Copy the line below into Terminal, press Return (no output means success), then open the app again:
install.warn4Text: In the blue SmartScreen dialog click More info, then Run anyway.

transcribe.importLead: You can bring audio and video in three ways:
transcribe.dragText: drop the file straight into the app window
transcribe.pickText: click Import file and choose it from disk
transcribe.urlText: paste a public video link and the app first resolves the title, duration and available qualities, then lets you choose between transcribing the audio and downloading the video. Some sites block hotlinking, so if it fails, use a local file instead. For the first time, read "Getting link transcription ready" below.
transcribe.urlPrepIntro: **yt-dlp**, which resolves and downloads the media, is already bundled in the installer, so there is nothing for you to install. When a site changes its rules you can fetch a newer component inside the app instead of reinstalling - see the "Can the link-resolution component update itself inside the app?" question in the FAQ. Link transcription also borrows a browser on your machine (Chrome / Edge / Chromium) to pass the site's front-end checks, so macOS asks for permission the first time you use it.
transcribe.urlPrep1Text: the transcription component ships with the app, so you can paste a link as soon as it is installed. If no browser is present, link resolution fails with a visible message - upload the local file in that case.
transcribe.urlPrep2Text: after you submit a link the system asks **"Vv Transcribe" wants to modify apps on this Mac.** - click **Allow…**. The app needs to launch your browser to complete the site check, and each Mac only has to allow it once. macOS restarts the app after you allow it; if it does not restart, quit it completely and open it again.
transcribe.urlPrep3Text: link transcription keeps failing. Open **System Settings → Privacy & Security → App Management**, find Vv Transcribe and switch it on, then restart the app.
transcribe.urlPrepNote: The browser only opens the page you pasted, using a fresh blank profile that the system creates in a temporary directory. **It does not read your account sign-in, passwords, bookmarks or browsing history.** Windows shows no such permission dialog - install the app and go.
transcribe.pickTitle: After resolving: transcribe the audio or download the video
transcribe.pickLead: A resolved link stops at a two-way choice, so you can read the quality list before committing - picking the wrong tier no longer means re-downloading the whole clip.
transcribe.pickAudioText: Only the audio track is fetched, usually a fraction of the same clip's size as a video, and it goes straight into transcription. Site cookies are deleted as soon as the audio is extracted; the temporary audio stays in the system temp folder so the player can replay each sentence, and is removed when the next clip starts or the app quits.
transcribe.pickVideoText: The video and audio tracks are merged into mp4 at the quality you picked, with progress measured from real bytes and a cancel button throughout. The system Save As dialog only appears once the download is complete, so cancelling never leaves a half-written file in your own folders; whether you save or cancel, the temporary copy is cleaned up.
transcribe.pickNote: The size on the card is the site's own estimate, so the real figure moves up or down. Videos behind a login or a paywall cannot be fetched, and live streams are refused outright. Download only material you are allowed to use - site terms and copyright are yours to judge.
transcribe.processText: After you click Start transcription, the Whisper engine runs speech recognition on your CPU, lines appear as they are produced, and progress follows the real position in the audio. You can cancel at any time. Speed depends on the length of the audio and your CPU, and the file is never uploaded to any server.
transcribe.tipText: the first transcription downloads the AI model weights for the tier you picked (Fast about 138MB, Precise about 461MB), so make sure you have network access. Later transcriptions use the locally cached model and need no network.
transcribe.timelineLead: The start and end times are now editable. There are two ways to change them - move the whole timeline at once, or fix one segment - and either way only the times move, the wording stays exactly as it is.
transcribe.timelineShiftText: Press **Timeline shift** in the toolbar above the segment list, type a number of seconds and press Apply: positive moves everything later, negative earlier, and all segments change in one action (the hint tells you how many segments there are and how far back you are allowed to go). Use it when the recording has a silent leader you need to move past. The limit is the earliest segment - it cannot be pushed before zero - and entering the opposite number takes you back exactly, with the gaps between segments unchanged.
transcribe.timelineSingleText: Double-click the time cell at the head of the row and two fields appear, "Start (s)" and "End (s)"; nothing lands until you press Save (Esc or Cancel leaves the times as they were). Right-clicking the row and choosing "Edit this segment's times" is the same path, and that menu carries two one-click items, **Set start or end to playhead**, which write the player's current position straight into that field - handy for lining a boundary up with the start of a shot.
transcribe.timelineUnitLabel: The unit is seconds, not timecode:
transcribe.timelineUnitText: Both fields and the shift field take seconds, decimals included (0.2 and 12.5 are fine), down to milliseconds. The line labelled "On-screen readout" shows the same whole-second clock the list uses, so don't sync to it by eye; the confirmation after a change reports seconds too, e.g. "This segment is now 20.5 → 27.7 s".
transcribe.timelineGateLabel: Bad values are refused on the spot:
transcribe.timelineGateText: The end must be later than the start (equal is a zero-length segment, reversed is a backwards one, and the app says which), the start cannot be before zero, before the previous segment's end or after the next segment's start - touching a neighbour is allowed, only overlap is refused. When it refuses, it names the limit in seconds and which neighbour to fix first. The reason for refusing rather than accepting is off-screen: the player highlights the first interval containing the playhead, so an overlapped segment would never light up, and the voice-over track is laid out in the same order - the symptom would show up on the audio much later, with nothing pointing back to that input box.
transcribe.timelineNoteText: Changing times is not changing text: the clip cache that landed in 1.1.4 keys on "this text plus these voice-over settings", so re-rendering after a timeline edit still re-synthesises only the segments whose wording you changed, and lays them out on the new timeline. Splitting, merging and deleting segments are not in 1.1.4 either - the number of segments and their text stay exactly as they are.
transcribe.tierTitle: Local model tiers: Fast and Precise
transcribe.tierLead: Transcription quality is now something you can choose. The tier only affects local transcription, and switching it leaves every other setting you have saved untouched.
transcribe.tierWhereText: **Settings → Transcription → Local model tier** - the option is only there while the transcription mode is set to local. After you save, the engine restarts once and every later transcription uses the new tier.
transcribe.tierFastText: about 138MB of weights; on our machine one minute of audio takes about 5-9 seconds. The price is Chinese homophone errors that change the meaning - the line 「英雄觉醒在即」 came back as 「英雄绝性在急」.
transcribe.tierExactText: about 461MB of weights; on the same machine it takes about 2.8x the Fast tier (one minute of audio in about 15-17 seconds) and hears that line correctly. If your captions go straight into a broadcast workflow where a wrong character costs you, use this tier.
transcribe.tierNoteText: each tier downloads its own weights the first time it is used (through hf-mirror.com in China), and switching does not delete the other tier, so plan disk space for both sizes above. When a switch or a first download fails, the splash screen and the transcription card show which stage you are in; if the engine does not come up, follow the "When the local engine fails to start" section below.
transcribe.langText: Pick it in the **Transcription language** dropdown under **Settings → Transcription**; it applies to every transcription after you save it, and the local engine and a cloud ASR API share the same setting. 12 languages are offered: Chinese (Mandarin), English, Japanese, Korean, Thai, Vietnamese, Indonesian, French, German, Spanish, Russian and Arabic. Chinese is the default.
transcribe.langNoAutoText: language detection picks the wrong language on accented or mixed-language material, and when it does the whole passage comes back translated - far harder to notice than a few wrong characters. So the app asks you to choose one language explicitly.
transcribe.langProofreadLabel: One caveat when you switch language:
transcribe.langProofreadText: local proofreading works from the misheard-homophone list and the Chinese dictionary, which only make sense for Chinese audio. Pick another language and one of two things happens: with a proofread model configured, the mode dialog still opens but "local proofreading" is greyed out and labelled "Chinese only"; with no model configured, no dialog appears at all - the app says this route does not apply and takes you straight to Settings → Proofread.
transcribe.engineTitle: When the local engine fails to start
transcribe.engineText: The app starts the local transcription engine itself, once, when the app boots. The first run downloads the model, so a network problem can make startup fail; the engine process can also be killed from outside - Activity Monitor, a cleanup script - and later transcriptions then get no answer. You do not have to quit the app: open **Settings → Transcription**, press **Check engine status** to see the current state, then press **Restart local engine** — the app reaps the engine that stopped answering and starts a fresh one. The button reads "Restarting..." while it works, which can take a minute or two on the first run while the model downloads.
transcribe.engineNoteText: Both buttons only exist while the transcription mode is set to local - switch it to cloud-first and they are replaced by a Test connection button that really calls the ASR endpoint. Pressing Restart local engine during a transcription is refused: stopping the engine would cut the stream the job is still reading, so the app tells you to let it finish or cancel first. Both buttons are also unclickable while a check or a restart is in flight. If restarts keep failing, collect the logs from Settings → About and updates → Open log folder, then reinstall the app.

reference.uploadLead: When transcription finishes, upload the broadcast or reference script to compare against it. The reference is used for a word-by-word comparison with the transcript so differences surface immediately.
reference.upload1: Click Upload reference and choose a TXT / Markdown / SRT / DOCX / PDF file (for legacy .doc, save it as .docx first)
reference.upload2: Only one reference script at a time; the button is disabled once one is uploaded
reference.upload3: To replace it, first click the clear button on the reference bubble

correction.lead: Click "Proofread" once the transcript is ready. If a proofread model is configured, a dialog lets you pick "local proofreading" or "AI proofreading". With no model and a Chinese transcript the dialog is skipped: local proofreading runs straight away and the button reads "本地校对中" (proofreading locally). A transcript in another language goes the other way - local proofreading does not apply there, see the language note under Transcription. A reference script is not a precondition - both modes work with or without one.
correction.item1Desc: No network, no tokens. It walks the transcript with the built-in list of misheard homophones (for example 以经 to 已经) and looks each result up in the bundled Chinese dictionary, so you can tell a recognition error from wording that was always correct. Those rules only hold for Chinese: pick another transcription language and, if a model is configured, "local proofreading" greys out in the dialog labelled "Chinese only"; with no model the dialog never opens and the app sends you to Settings → Proofread instead.
correction.item2Desc: Calls the third-party model you filled in under Settings → Proofread and reads the sentence in context: with a reference script it explains every difference against it, without one it scans the transcript for suspicious spots. Needs a connection and spends a few tokens.
correction.item3Title: Suggestions only - you approve each one
correction.item3Desc: Neither mode rewrites your subtitles. Each difference comes with an explanation and waits for you to click Accept; if the reference script itself contains a mistake, such as a typo, it is flagged for your judgement as well.
correction.noteText: while a proofreading run is in progress the clear button on the reference script is disabled, so an accidental click cannot interrupt the analysis.

voice.lead: Voice-over is the third tab at the top of the home screen. Inside it is two panels: the left one is three controls from top to bottom - pick a profile (on the cloud tier that is the whole "voice-over profile": endpoint plus key plus model; on the local tier this slot picks which model, VITS or Kokoro), pick a voice, set the speed. Under that column, since 1.1.2 the cloud tier also has a "Voice cloning" entry, which only shows up for MiniMax and Alibaba Cloud Model Studio. The right one carries a single state - idle, synthesizing, done. The script is synthesized segment by segment, then assembled into one track by FFmpeg on your machine - the voice-over step leaves your subtitles and their timing alone.
voice.item1Desc: "Plain text" takes whatever you type or paste. "From transcription" uses the non-empty segments of the current transcript and shows the segment and character counts as they are; edit the wording on the transcription page, because this panel reads them unchanged.
voice.item2Desc: Press "Audition first line" before running the whole batch: it reads the first segment of that batch. A wrong vendor, API base, key or voice model surfaces here instead of at segment 20 of a long script. Whether the voice slot may stay empty depends on the vendor: MiniMax, Alibaba Cloud Model Studio and Doubao need one, so "Start voice-over" stops you before anything is sent, while on the OpenAI-compatible tier it is optional - and if you do fill one that the model rejects, the line you get back is the endpoint's own wording.
voice.item3Title: Cloud API, or synthesis on your machine
voice.item3Desc: Both tiers share the same page and the same assembly path. Since 1.1.2 the cloud tier knows four vendors, and the "Vendor" field inside the profile decides what the request looks like: OpenAI-compatible, MiniMax, Alibaba Cloud Model Studio (CosyVoice) and Doubao (Volcano Engine) - different path, different body, different auth header, different response shape, while everything after that (writing the MP3, measuring duration, laying the track, joining, keeping the tally) is one code path. Which gateway and which voice model travel together as a profile (vendor / API base URL / API key / voice model - picking Doubao adds a fifth field, the resource id, which says which version of the synthesis service your account bought and is neither a model nor a secret; since 1.1.0 the voice id is no longer part of it), so on the page you just pick a profile and your provider bills each call. The base URL only needs the scheme and the host; the app appends the path for the vendor you chose. Pasting the whole endpoint from their documentation works too - that exact URL is then what gets called. The voice slot now comes in two shapes: for MiniMax the app fetches a list with the key you configured and hangs it under the field as a dropdown - system voices plus the ones you cloned yourself (those are labelled "cloned"), filtered as you type, one click fills the field. When the list cannot be fetched, or the vendor has no list endpoint at all, the field is typed by hand as before, the hint says why this time, and it links to that vendor's own voice list page (the OpenAI-compatible tier publishes none, so nothing is linked there). The local tier synthesizes on your machine: no API call, no cost. Since 1.0.7 the local tier has two models to pick from: VITS (small, fewer voices) - about 135.5MB with 5 voices - and Kokoro (large, many voices) - about 426.6MB with 103 voices. Neither publishes voice names upstream, so you tell them apart by ear. Cloud or local is saved under Settings → Voice-over; the model slot on the page changes only the batch you are about to run and never writes back to settings.
voice.item4Title: One call per segment, with the tally on screen
voice.item4Desc: Calls run serially and the progress follows real segment numbers ("X of N synthesized"), and the page states the count before you press start, along with whether your provider bills it. Empty segments are skipped; three consecutive failures stop the batch; you can cancel mid-run and everything already synthesized still assembles into a track. But cancel only stops the segments after it - the one in flight and the request already sent cannot be recalled, and once assembly starts the cancel button disappears.
voice.item5Title: Laid out on the subtitle timeline
voice.item5Desc: With "From transcription", each clip starts where its subtitle starts. If a clip is longer than its slot it is pushed later and the rest of the track follows - nothing is truncated, nothing is layered on top of each other. The result panel reports how much longer the track is than the original timeline and how many segments were pushed. "Plain text" has no timeline: the clips are read one after another.
voice.item6Desc: The output is a 44.1 kHz mono MP3 you can play back on the page before pressing "Save track" to write it anywhere through the system Save dialog. If you never save it, clearing the batch or starting a new one deletes it; a copy already saved elsewhere is untouched. The subtitle file itself is unaffected - export works exactly as before.
voice.noteText: Three things to know. (1) On the cloud tier, the vendor, the API base and the key belong to the profile marked "In use" under Settings → Voice-over; leaving the base and key empty reuses what Proofread already saved, but that only reads true when the vendor field says OpenAI-compatible - with MiniMax, Model Studio or Doubao selected an empty base is usually just the wrong place. The voice model is never reused - pointing that audio endpoint at a chat model gets rejected outright. Providers that only offer chat usually do not have this audio endpoint - check their documentation. Each segment sends caption text (never your media file), plus the voice id when you filled one, to the address you configured. The "Voice cloning" step is the exception: what leaves your machine there is the recording you picked. (2) The local tier needs two on-demand components - the engine program and the model for the tier you pick - and neither ships inside the installer. Since 1.0.7 both can be downloaded under Settings → About and updates → On-demand components: the engine comes from this repository's publicly released assets, listed in a component manifest we maintain and verified per file against SHA2-256, while the model is fetched from hf-mirror.com by the commit and per-file sha256 pinned in the code (about 135.5MB for VITS, 426.6MB for Kokoro). Once both pieces are installed, only the download touches the network - afterwards synthesis never leaves your machine, because the engine only listens on 127.0.0.1 - and the first synthesis waits a little longer while the engine process starts and the model loads into memory. (3) The "Experimental" badge sits on the tab rather than only on the local tier: voice-over getting its own page and on-device synthesis both arrived in v1.0.6, and the assembly path the two tiers share still has not been walked end to end on packaged Intel Mac and Windows builds as of 1.1.2, so the badge stays. Since 1.0.8 CI does launch the voice-over engine binary on each of the three platforms and checks that its native libraries were collected (first run 2026-10-30, all three green) - but that proves the engine layer only; the assembly path, the interface and the installer are not inside that green. "Voice-over does not modify your subtitles or their timing" is the line this release holds; if the track does not line up, use "Audition first line" and the counters on the result panel to find out why.
voice.item7Title: Build a voice from your own recording
voice.item7Desc: Since 1.1.2 the cloud tier has a "Voice cloning" entry under the voice-over controls (the local tier has no such thing - it only speaks the voices that ship with the engine). It opens a dialog: step 1 is "Pick a recording", which only selects the file and sends nothing yet; the name field in step 2 is filled in for you once the file is picked, and you can change it; the button at the bottom right is "Start cloning", and pressing it is when the audio actually leaves your machine. What length, size and format each vendor accepts is shown in the dialog in their own words. Whether the app can build a voice comes down to one thing: whether the voice-over key you saved in settings reaches that vendor's enrollment endpoint. MiniMax does - the recording is uploaded first to get a file id, then used to create the voice, and the voice id is yours to name. Alibaba Cloud Model Studio does too - the audio goes out as Base64 inside the request, you only supply a name prefix and the full voice name is assembled on their side. Doubao and the OpenAI-compatible tier do not show the entry at all: Doubao requires buying a voice slot in its console first, which this key cannot do, and the OpenAI specification has no such endpoint. The "This call goes to" line in the dialog lists the endpoints the main process actually derived - cloning uses different paths than synthesis - and the "Change address" button beside it applies to this call only and is never written back to settings. When it succeeds, the new voice id drops straight into the "Voice" slot on the voice-over page with a toast. Two things to keep in mind: this step sends the recording you picked to the provider's server, and the voice you created stays in that account as a long-term asset - this app cannot delete it, only their console can.
voice.item8Title: Fix a few words and the new version only costs the segments you changed
voice.item8Desc: Since 1.1.4 there is a clip cache in front of the per-segment synthesis loop: one line of text plus one set of "how it is spoken" parameters (engine tier, vendor or local engine, voice model, voice, speed - and for the cloud tier also the API base and Doubao's resource id) equals one audio file. Reading the same line with the same parameters again reuses that file, with no API call and no cost - so a 300-segment script with 3 characters corrected really sends 3 calls. You can see this in the interface: while the batch runs, a reused segment reports "Segment N reused the audio synthesized earlier, no API call", and the counter on the result panel reads "X segments reused with no API call, Y newly synthesized". Both numbers are stored with that history record too. Rotating the API key does not invalidate the cache - it changes nothing about how a line sounds, and counting it would throw away an entire cache for nothing; "Audition first line" and the "Test connection" button deliberately skip the cache as well, because their job is to verify the endpoint and the voice right now, and caching them would turn a self-check into something that never looks at what the other side returned. The cache lives in the app's own user-data directory - not under the temp folder that is swept at every launch (no reuse would ever happen there) and not in the history layer (that one holds deliverables you chose to keep). So the "Voice-over clip cache" row under Settings → About and updates reports "N segments, X on disk" and carries a "Clear cache" button, and clearing it is refused with a reason while a batch is running. Any failure in this layer is treated as a miss - if a file cannot be moved into the cache, the temporary file is used as it is - this layer should never make a synthesis fail.

export.lead: When proofreading is done, click Export and the system Save dialog lets you pick the format and location:
export.srtDesc: The standard subtitle format, with timing, ready to import into video editing software
export.vttDesc: The WebVTT subtitle format, read directly by browser players and YouTube
export.tsvDesc: One line per sentence with its timecode in front - handy as a voice-over script and it opens in any spreadsheet
export.txtDesc: Plain text, easy to copy, paste and edit further
export.jsonDesc: Keeps timing and per-line structure for automated pipelines
export.mdDesc: A script with time markers, good for archiving and review

history.lead: The entry point is the icon beside Settings in the title bar - the same one opens and closes it - and the panel is a drawer floating on the right, so it never resizes the view underneath. Inside are four tabs, All / Transcription / Downloads / Voice-over, each with its own count, and the icon next to the title re-reads the ledger from disk.
history.item1Desc: Transcription, video download and voice-over each write a row the moment they finish - there is no Save button to press. A row reads "time · cloud, or which local model · N segments · source length"; a voice-over row also says "12/300 segments", and hovering it adds the voice id, the speed, the track size and how many segments were pushed later. "Finished" and "stopped halfway" used to look identical here.
history.item2Desc: What lands on disk is the metadata of that job: which tier, cloud or which local model, segment count, durations, elapsed time, product size. Not one character of the transcript - unless you tick "Keep script" on that row.
history.item3Title: "Keep" is the only thing that survives
history.item3Desc: Products you did not keep sit in a temp directory and are swept after 24 hours; ticking Keep copies them into records/keep/ inside your own user data directory, outside that sweep. A row whose original has already been swept cannot be ticked, and the panel says so.
history.item4Desc: The ledger holds at most 200 rows, and when it overflows it drops the oldest row that has nothing kept. The kept side has no cap, so the footer states "N kept, X in total" and, past 2GB, names the biggest one. That sentence only counts - it never deletes anything for you.
history.item5Title: Three things a row can do
history.item5Desc: Tick Keep (on a transcription row it is labelled "Keep script"); press Show to select that copy in Finder / Explorer; press Delete to remove the row together with whatever it kept, after one confirmation. Unticking only gives back the copy - the row itself stays.
history.item6Title: After a restart the text is gone
history.item6Desc: A transcription row keeps no audio (the extracted audio is cleaned at the completion point), so the only full text it can keep is the script - and that lives only in the interface of that session. Once the app restarts, the row can no longer reach it. The panel says this plainly; that sentence is the whole content of the "full text on demand" promise.
history.noteText: The interface asks for row ids and never receives a path: where the original product lives, and where records/keep/ lives, are known only to the main process, and "Show in folder" is the single control that touches the file manager. If the ledger cannot be read, the drawer says it cannot be read rather than "you have not run anything yet". History and kept copies live in your own user data directory, ship in no installer and are uploaded nowhere.

api.aboutText: Transcription uses the local Whisper engine bundled inside the app; while the transcription mode stays on local it needs no network and produces no API cost. Local proofreading is the same - it only consults the built-in misheard-word list and the Chinese dictionary, so it works without a key. AI proofreading depends on a third-party model: fill in your own API key under Settings → Proofread. For a Chinese transcript with no key, clicking Proofread simply runs the local pass and tells you where to configure it; for another language that route does not apply, so the app points you at the proofread settings instead. You can also switch the transcription mode to cloud under Settings → Transcription and use a third-party ASR API in place of the local engine - since 1.1.2 the cloud tier knows three vendors: OpenAI-compatible, MiniMax, and iFlytek's large-model recording-file transcription (that one has no model field at all; in its place you fill AppID and APISecret, and the secret is encrypted with your system keystore exactly like a key). That same tab holds the transcription language and the engine's health: if the engine stops answering, press Check engine status and then Restart local engine - no need to quit the app. Voice-over has its own tab, Settings → Voice-over, where you first pick "Cloud API (default)" or "Local voice-over (needs the engine and model downloaded)": what the cloud tier manages here is the list of voice-over profiles: one profile holds the vendor, the API base URL, the API key and the voice model - that first field decides the shape of the request, and since 1.1.2 offers OpenAI-compatible, MiniMax, Alibaba Cloud Model Studio (CosyVoice) and Doubao (Volcano Engine); choosing Doubao adds a fifth field, the resource id - edited in the dialog that a row opens and written to disk by the Save button inside that dialog. Leave the base URL and key empty and it reuses the proofreading ones, which is only a meaningful shortcut when the vendor says OpenAI-compatible; the voice model is never shared - pointing an audio endpoint at a chat model gets rejected, while Doubao is the opposite case and expects that field empty for its system voices. Since 1.1.0 the voice id is not in this tab and not bound to a profile: you pick it per batch on the voice-over page, and whether it may stay empty depends on the vendor - MiniMax, Model Studio and Doubao need one, so "Start voice-over" stops you before anything is sent, while the OpenAI-compatible tier treats it as optional. The local tier needs no key because it synthesizes on your machine. Both tiers have Test connection: the cloud one speaks a ten-character sentence to prove the vendor, base, key and voice model all work (the voice id is not filled on this tab, so for MiniMax the probe substitutes a system voice the app has actually heard and says so in the result; for Doubao it uses the first entry of the official 2.0 voice list - there is no key for that vendor on this machine, so that line is built to their documentation rather than measured; for Model Studio it will not guess an id it has no source for, so it states that this page cannot test that vendor and sends you to the voice-over page to fill a voice and audition; on the OpenAI-compatible tier it sends whatever the settings already hold - and omits the field entirely when that is empty too), and the local one speaks it through the tier you picked, telling you which piece is missing if the engine or the model is not downloaded yet.
api.profilesText: Transcription, proofreading and voice-over each keep their own list - up to 3 profiles per capability, each with one "In use" pointer. A profile holds only the things you change when you switch vendor: it starts with the vendor dropdown ("Vendor" for transcription and voice-over, "Provider" for proofreading), followed by whatever credentials that vendor needs. What is in each dropdown: transcription - OpenAI-compatible, MiniMax and iFlytek (large-model recording-file transcription); voice-over - OpenAI-compatible, MiniMax, Alibaba Cloud Model Studio (CosyVoice) and Doubao (Volcano Engine); proofreading - OpenAI, DeepSeek, Qwen and a custom OpenAI-compatible endpoint. How many fields you get depends on the vendor: OpenAI-compatible, MiniMax and the proofreading providers take base URL / key / model; iFlytek has no model field and takes AppID and APISecret in its place; Doubao voice-over adds a resource id on top of the model field. AppID and the resource id are stored in plain text because they are parameters the request sends, while APISecret and every key go through the system keystore. Switching the vendor in the transcription and voice-over lists clears the fields below it, because the app will not guess an address or a model name for you; the proofreading list does the opposite and fills in a base URL and a default model, which you can still overwrite. Everything else stays global: the transcription mode (cloud-first or local), the local model size, the transcription language, the voice-over engine (cloud or local), the speed and the voice id. Those are not "another vendor" differences - folding them into a profile is how you get the coupling where picking a profile silently moves your settings.
api.profile1Desc: The Edit button on a row opens a dialog where the credential fields live, and Save inside that dialog writes that profile immediately; the Save settings button at the bottom of the tab covers only the global fields and never touches the list. A list may also be empty - picking cloud with no profile is blocked with a message telling you to press "New API connection".
api.profile2Desc: A profile takes its name from the model when it is created and there is no rename control: the row already shows "model · host", and a private alias nobody else can read only makes the list harder to scan.
api.profile3Desc: The "In use" mark in the settings list (a checkbox in that dialog, written with the same Save), and the profile dropdown carried by the transcription page, the proofreading dialog and the voice-over page. They move the same pointer, so switching on the voice-over page is exactly what you see back in Settings.
api.profile4Desc: The API key is encrypted with your system keystore (macOS Keychain / Windows DPAPI) before it reaches disk, and the interface only receives three states - present, usable, plaintext - never the value itself. When the keystore cannot read it back (another machine, or the keystore was cleared) the row says exactly that; type the key again and save.
api.vendor4Desc: Any API that speaks the OpenAI format
api.vendor5Desc: Since 1.1.1 both transcription and cloud voice-over (transcription model like asr-1.0, voice model like speech-2.8-hd). Since 1.1.2 this vendor also supports cloning a voice in the app, and the candidate list under the voice slot on the voice-over page is fetched from it
api.vendor6Desc: Cloud voice-over only; its transcription API is not wired up in this release - it takes a public audio URL and polls a job. Since 1.1.2 this vendor can also clone a voice in the app
api.step1: Open the app and go to Settings → Proofread (for cloud transcription, use Transcription instead; for voice-over, use Voice-over)
api.step2: In the profile list press "New API connection" (or Edit on an existing row): the first field picks the vendor ("Vendor" for transcription and voice-over, "Provider" for proofreading), then fill in the fields below it from their documentation. Switching that dropdown clears the fields below it in the transcription and voice-over lists - the app will not fill in values it would have to guess. iFlytek asks for API base URL / APIKey / AppID / APISecret and has no model field, and Doubao voice-over adds a resource id next to the model field.
api.step3: Press Test connection first - it sends a real request with what you have typed, before saving, so you know this profile works
api.step4: Then press Save inside that dialog and the profile lands on disk - "Set as current" is a checkbox in the same dialog. The global fields (transcription mode, local model size, language, voice-over engine) still need Save settings at the bottom of the settings page
api.step5: Back on the home screen, import a file and transcribe it, then click Proofread and pick AI to verify the configuration; a missing key or a failed call both show a visible message
api.noteText: third-party APIs charge their own fees, billed by the vendor and unrelated to Vv Transcribe. With no API configured, local transcription, reference comparison, local proofreading, on-device voice-over and export all still work; only AI proofreading, cloud transcription and cloud-tier voice-over require a key.
api.vendor7Desc: Cloud voice-over only since 1.1.2 (the v3 one-way streaming endpoint, plus a resource id field like seed-tts-2.0); transcription is not wired up - it too requires a public audio URL
api.vendor8Desc: Cloud transcription only since 1.1.2 (the large-model recording-file API: upload, get an order id, poll for the result), and it needs three credentials - AppID / APIKey / APISecret; voice-over is not wired up

net.q: Do I need a network connection the first time?
net.a: Once: the first transcription downloads the Whisper model weights for the tier you picked - about 138MB for Fast, about 461MB for Precise (in China this goes through the hf-mirror.com mirror). The two pieces on-device voice-over needs - the engine program and the model - are not in the installer either; since 1.0.7 both can be downloaded under Settings → About and updates → On-demand components. Once those are cached, local transcription, comparison, local proofreading and export need no network at all, and voice-over synthesis never leaves the machine either once the engine is installed (it only listens on 127.0.0.1). AI proofreading and cloud-tier voice-over call the third-party API you configured, so they always need a connection.

language.a: Twelve: Chinese (Mandarin), English, Japanese, Korean, Thai, Vietnamese, Indonesian, French, German, Spanish, Russian and Arabic. Choose one explicitly in the Transcription language dropdown under Settings → Transcription and save it; Chinese is the default. There is no auto-detect - it picks the wrong language on accented or mixed-language material, and when it does the whole passage comes back translated. Remember that local proofreading only covers Chinese, so for other languages use AI proofreading.

engine.q: The local engine did not start and transcription keeps failing - what now?
engine.a: You do not have to quit the app. Open Settings → Transcription and press Check engine status - it tells you whether the engine answers normally, does not answer at all, or is online but on an older protocol (usually a leftover engine from the previous generation still holding port 8000). Then press Restart local engine: the app reaps the dead process and starts a fresh one, showing "Restarting..." while it works (a minute or two on the first run, when the model still has to download). Press it during a transcription and it is refused - stopping the engine would cut off the job that is still streaming, so the app asks you to wait for it or cancel. If restarts keep failing, take the logs from Settings → About and updates → Open log folder and reinstall the app.

appManagement.q: My Mac asks "Vv Transcribe" wants to modify apps on this Mac. when I transcribe a link - what do I do?
appManagement.a: Click Allow… - each Mac only has to do this once. Link transcription launches your local Chrome or Edge to open the page you pasted so the site check can pass, and macOS classifies that as App Management, hence the dialog. After you allow it the system restarts the app; if you denied it earlier, switch Vv Transcribe on under System Settings → Privacy & Security → App Management and restart the app. This step does not read your browser accounts, passwords or history.

urlFailed.a: Since v1.0.2 yt-dlp is bundled in the installer, so you no longer have to install it and a failure is rarely a missing component. If the message says the link-resolution process was interrupted by the system, the bundled yt-dlp has not been allowed to run - permit Vv Transcribe under System Settings → Privacy & Security and try again. If it is another permission problem, use the Open privacy settings button in the dialog. Some sites block hotlinking or require a login, so resolution can still fail - in that case upload the media you downloaded as a local file. A link that downloads fine but then fails to transcribe is an engine problem; see the "The local engine did not start" question above.

component.q: Can the link-resolution component update itself inside the app?
component.a: Yes - since v1.0.4 you do not have to reinstall the whole package for it. Open Settings → About and updates; the link-resolution row shows the version and size this machine is using. Press Check for updates, and when the manifest lists a newer version an "Update to X" button appears - press it and the download starts. The update only replaces the app's own copy, the version bundled in the installer stays untouched, and if the download or the checksum fails it falls back to the copy you had, keeps showing the old version and tells you in a visible message. The manifest is maintained by this project itself, every entry checked against the upstream file fingerprint, and it is only ever fetched from our own repository. Since v1.0.6 this list also carries the two voice-over pieces - the engine program and the model for the tier you pick (about 135.5MB for VITS, 426.6MB for Kokoro) - and they are not bundled in the installer. Since 1.0.7 both rows can be pressed: the engine comes from our own manifest and the Release assets behind it with a SHA2-256 check per file, the model from hf-mirror.com by the commit and per-file sha256 pinned in the code. Once both pieces are in, you can delete them again to reclaim the space, and when one is missing the voice-over page says exactly which piece is missing instead of failing after the fact.

ttsVendor.q: How do I connect a new vendor for cloud voice-over, and how much of the URL should the base field hold?
ttsVendor.a: Open Settings → Voice-over and press "New API connection" in the voice-over profile list (or Edit on an existing row). The first field, "Vendor", picks one of four: OpenAI-compatible, MiniMax, Alibaba Cloud Model Studio (CosyVoice) or Doubao (Volcano Engine). Choosing one clears the fields below it - the app will not guess an address or a model name, so fill the API base URL, API key and voice model from their documentation (Doubao also asks for a resource id, shaped like seed-tts-2.0, and its voice model field is correctly left empty for system voices). Then press Save at the bottom of the dialog, which writes to disk immediately. The base URL only needs the scheme and the host (for MiniMax, something like https://api.minimax.cn); the app appends the endpoint path for the vendor you chose. Pasting the whole endpoint from their documentation works too - that exact URL is then what gets called. A 404 from Test connection or from voice-over usually means this field has one path segment too many or too few; 401 means the key is wrong, expired, or not allowed to call that model; a 200 whose body is not a JSON object (typically an HTML error page from the gateway) is the same field pointing at the wrong layer. The transcription APIs of Model Studio and Doubao take only a public audio URL and poll a job, so this release wires up their voice-over and not their transcription; iFlytek is the mirror case - transcription only. Model names and voice ids follow each vendor's documentation: the voice field is required for MiniMax, Model Studio and Doubao, so "Start voice-over" stops you before anything is sent when it is empty. For MiniMax the app also fetches a list with your key and hangs it under the field as a dropdown (the voices you cloned yourself are in it, labelled "cloned"); Model Studio and Doubao have no list-voices endpoint, so the hint under that field links to each of their own system voice lists instead, which you can copy from; MiniMax falls back to that same link when the list cannot be fetched. OpenAI-compatible has no public list, so nothing is linked there.

tempFiles.q: Does the media stay on my computer while I transcribe or download?
tempFiles.a: Only briefly, and every piece has a defined cleanup point. Link imports land in the system temp folder: site cookies are deleted the moment the audio is extracted; the temporary audio stays while the player replays it and is removed when the next clip starts or the app quits; a downloaded video is removed as soon as you pick where to save it, or cancel the save. Changing the link, switching back to the local file tab, or closing the uploader releases that folder immediately. Voice-over clips and the assembled track get their own temp folder too: pressing Clear on the result panel, or starting a new batch (which recycles the previous batch first), deletes it - a copy you already saved elsewhere is untouched. If the app is force-quit and misses the cleanup, the next start sweeps temp folders older than 24 hours. Nothing is ever uploaded.

accuracy.a: Accuracy depends heavily on audio quality, accent and how many proper nouns appear, so we do not publish a percentage we have not measured. For zero-tolerance use such as broadcast captions, always run reference comparison together with local or AI proofreading as a second pass instead of trusting the raw recognition result.

security.a: Transcription, reference comparison, local proofreading and on-device voice-over run entirely on your machine; audio and video are never uploaded to any server. If you enable cloud transcription, AI proofreading or cloud-tier voice-over, the audio or the caption text is sent to the third-party API you configured yourself, under that provider's privacy policy - voice-over sends caption text segment by segment, never the media file. The local voice-over tier calls no API at all: your caption text stays on the machine, and only the one-time engine and model download touches the network.

speed.a: The local engine runs int8 inference on your CPU and does not use a GPU, so speed is mostly a function of audio length, CPU performance and the tier you picked: on our machine one minute of audio takes about 5-9 seconds on Fast and about 15-17 seconds on Precise (about 2.8x). The first transcription also waits for the model to download and load; the splash screen and the transcription card show which stage you are in. If it feels too slow, switch the tier back down under Settings → Transcription - no reinstall needed.

feedback.q: How do I report a problem?
feedback.a: Open Settings → About and updates → Feedback and press Send feedback email: your mail client opens with the recipient, the app version, your system information and where the logs live already filled in, so all you have to write is which step failed, what media you used and what you expected. Copy email address is there too if you would rather write it yourself. On the same tab, Open log folder shows you the .log files - attaching them tells us far more than the words "the transcription is wrong". To look it up yourself first, the same tab also has Help documentation, whose Open user guide button brings you to this page - the guide lives online only, so it changes without reinstalling the app.

cancel.q: Can I stop a transcription partway?
cancel.a: Yes. The transcription card has a Cancel button; clicking it aborts the job and releases the engine, so you can start again with another file or another mode.

ads.q: How does the website make money? Are there ads or tracking in the app?
ads.a: There are no ads in the app, and no tracking or telemetry - you can check that claim: the repository is public, and the app only ever makes three kinds of outbound request while running: the API provider you configure yourself in Settings, the model download source (hf-mirror.com), and the public GitHub endpoints used for update checks and on-demand components (api.github.com / raw.githubusercontent.com / github.com). Nothing leaves your machine outside those three, and there is no "send it back to us" category, because we run no server that receives user data. The website is funded by page advertising: the ad slots on vvscribe.com come from Google AdSense, and ads stay on the web page - never in the app. Once this site starts serving ads, the first time you visit you are asked once whether you accept ad cookies; if you decline or choose "Necessary only", the page never loads the ad script, and the Cookie settings link in the footer lets you change your mind at any time. The full wording is in the "This website and advertising" section of the privacy policy.

referenceFormat.q: Which reference script formats are supported?
referenceFormat.a: Five: TXT, Markdown, SRT, DOCX and PDF. For legacy .doc, save it as .docx in Word first. Only one script at a time; to change it, click the clear button on the reference bubble first.

update.q: How do I get a new version?
update.a: The app does not install updates by itself (it is not code-signed). In Settings → About and updates, click Check for updates to see whether a newer build exists, then follow the link to the release page and install over the top. Only the link-resolution component can be refreshed without reinstalling the whole package - see the "Can the link-resolution component update itself inside the app?" question above.

slowDownload.q: Downloading from the site or GitHub is very slow - what can I do?
slowDownload.a: The installers live in GitHub Releases, and from China the GitHub asset domain has no CDN acceleration, so throughput can drop to a few tens of KB/s and a several-hundred-MB package takes a long time. We do not offer third-party mirrors - a mirror of unknown origin may have been modified and we cannot vouch for its safety. The reliable approach: turn on network acceleration and download the links on this page with your browser. On macOS, Homebrew works too (it also goes through GitHub, but it resumes interrupted downloads and retries more reliably than a browser). When Check for updates cannot reach the release page, it copies the release URL to your clipboard so you can paste it into a browser.

voiceClone.q: How do I delete a voice I cloned from a recording?
voiceClone.a: The app cannot. Cloning creates a voice inside the account of whichever vendor you configured, and from then on it is a long-term asset of that account: the voice list the voice-over page fetches keeps showing it (labelled "cloned" on MiniMax), and switching key or vendor shows you a different set. To delete it, use that vendor's console or its own API. Two more things: this step sends the recording you picked to the provider's server - MiniMax receives it as an upload that returns a file id, Model Studio receives it as Base64 inside the request - and the app only calls the "create" endpoint. It never calls a delete endpoint, so it will not touch anything already in your account.

privacy.title: Privacy policy
privacy.overviewText: Vv Transcribe ("the App") is a local subtitle transcription and proofreading tool for media professionals. This policy has two halves, because they describe two completely different things. **1. The App** - the program installed on your computer. Its core principle is that **everything is processed locally by default**, and data leaves your machine only for a provider you chose yourself, after you configure a third-party API; the four sections below ("Data processed on your machine", "API configuration", "Information we collect" and "Model download") are all about it. **2. This website, vvscribe.com** - the page you are reading in a browser. Once it starts serving ads it places ad cookies in the visitor's browser, which has nothing to do with the app, so it is written up separately in the "This website and advertising" section. Merging the two into one sentence that says "we collect no personal information" would be false, so we do not write it that way.
privacy.local1: Audio and video transcription in local mode runs entirely on your machine; files are never uploaded to any server
privacy.local2: Reference comparison, local proofreading and on-device voice-over run on your machine and never upload your broadcast script or caption text
privacy.local3: Transcripts and subtitle files are stored only on your device
privacy.apiLead: AI proofreading only runs once you configure a third-party AI API (such as OpenAI or Qwen); local proofreading needs no API configuration at all. Cloud-tier voice-over reuses that same API base and key (you can also set them separately under Voice-over - leaving them empty means reuse), and the profile also carries the voice model (since 1.1.2 a voice-over profile is four fields: vendor / API base URL / API key / voice model, and the vendor is OpenAI-compatible, MiniMax, Alibaba Cloud Model Studio (CosyVoice) or Doubao (Volcano Engine) - Doubao adds a resource id). The voice id is not bound to a profile - you pick it per batch on the voice-over page, where MiniMax, Model Studio and Doubao require one and the OpenAI-compatible tier leaves it optional, and whatever you type there goes out with that segment of caption text. Whether your provider has the endpoint is up to its own documentation. Voice-over also has an on-device tier that calls no API at all. If you also switch the transcription mode under Transcription configuration to cloud, transcription requests your chosen endpoint as well (that profile's vendor can be OpenAI-compatible, MiniMax or iFlytek; iFlytek asks for three credentials - AppID, APIKey and APISecret - and the secret is only used locally to sign each request, never sent). In that case:
privacy.api1: Caption text (AI proofreading, cloud-tier voice-over) or audio (cloud transcription) is sent to the third-party API provider you configured; voice-over sends caption text segment by segment and never the media file. The "Voice cloning" step added in 1.1.2 is the exception: there, what leaves your machine is the recording you picked - MiniMax receives it as an upload that returns a file id, Alibaba Cloud Model Studio receives it as Base64 inside the request - and only those two vendors can reach this path at all
privacy.api2: Processing of that data is governed by that provider's own privacy policy
privacy.api3: Your API key and, for iFlytek, the APISecret are stored only on your own device and are never uploaded; before they are written to disk they are encrypted with your system keystore (the macOS Keychain / Windows DPAPI), and only if that keystore is unavailable does it fall back to plain text - in which case Settings says so explicitly, marking whether the secret is currently encrypted or not. The iFlytek AppID and the Doubao voice-over resource id are parameters the request sends rather than credentials, so they are stored in plain text
privacy.collectLead: This section is about the App. The App collects no personal information and runs no server of ours that receives user data (the website is a different matter - see "This website and advertising" below). The following is stored on your own device only:
privacy.collect3: Usage logs (stored on this machine only, for troubleshooting; since 1.0.8 they go through a single write path that, before anything reaches disk, strips credentials such as API keys, tokens and cookies and the fields carrying your transcript text, and reduces absolute paths to file names; each file is capped at 5MB with at most 4 kept, so the log cannot grow without bound)
privacy.collect4: History records (stored on this machine only since 1.0.9: finishing a transcription, download or voice-over job writes one row of metadata - tier, cloud or which local model, segment count, durations, product size - into records/history.json inside your user data directory, at most 200 rows. The script text and the audio track are copied into records/keep/ only when you tick "Keep" on that row; unticked products disappear with the 24-hour temp sweep. Nothing leaves your machine and there is no reporting of any kind)
privacy.modelText: On the first transcription the App downloads the Whisper weights for the tier you chose from the hf-mirror.com mirror: about 138MB for Fast (base) and about 461MB for Precise (small). Each tier downloads only when it is first used, and the files then stay in the local Hugging Face cache (~/.cache/huggingface/hub on macOS and Linux), so there is no repeat download. That exchange carries model files only and uploads no user data. The two on-demand voice-over components work the same way: each model tier is fetched from hf-mirror.com by the commit and per-file sha256 pinned in the code, and the engine program comes from this repository's publicly released assets, listed in a component manifest we maintain and verified per file against SHA2-256. Either way files come down, nothing of yours goes up.
privacy.siteLead: Everything above is about the app installed on your computer. This section is only about **the page you are on**: it has no accounts, no forms and no backend, and these are the only things it does inside a visitor's browser.
privacy.site1: Visit statistics: the page loads the Cloudflare Web Analytics counting script (from static.cloudflareinsights.com). It counts from the browser's own performance metrics, **sets no cookie** and does no cross-site tracking; what we see is aggregate numbers such as pageviews, referrer and an approximate region - never who you are
privacy.site2: Advertising: this site is funded by page advertising, and the ad slots come from Google AdSense - ads appear on this web page only, never inside the app. Once the ad script is loaded, Google stores and reads its own cookies in your browser (identifiers such as IDE and test_cookie) to serve, deduplicate and measure those ads, and the request also carries the address of the page you are viewing together with browser information. Google processes those cookies under its own policy; this site cannot read those values out of your browser and never sells visitor data to anyone
privacy.site3: Consent and withdrawal: until you see the banner and choose "Accept ads", the page **does not load the ad script**, so no ad cookie exists; choosing "Necessary only" also leaves it unloaded. That choice lives in this browser's localStorage only, and the site sets no cookie for it. The Cookie settings link in the footer lets you change your mind at any time - the banner and the ad slot only ever appear once this site actually starts serving ads
privacy.site4: One limitation we should state plainly: that banner is something this site implements itself. It only decides whether the ad script is loaded; it is **not a Google-certified consent management platform (CMP) and produces no IAB TCF consent string**. So in the European Economic Area and the United Kingdom, even when a visitor accepts, Google only serves non-personalised ads, which pay less than personalised ones. That is not a breach of policy, but without a certified CMP that revenue is simply out of reach; running personalised ads would mean integrating a certified CMP first, which is a later commercial decision - if we take it, we will correct this section before anything changes
privacy.site5: Hosting and transport: the site is hosted on Cloudflare Pages, and the domain and DNS are with Cloudflare too. As the host, Cloudflare processes a visitor's IP address as far as providing the service requires (routing, abuse prevention, rate limiting and its own access logs). Apart from the items above, this site sends no visitor information to any service of ours - we have no such service
